title: Affine realization of supplied relative dualizing pairs without Noetherian assumptions
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated flat locally finitely presented morphism of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $(K,\xi),(L,\eta)$ be supplied coherent relative dualizing pairs [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ be affine opens with $f(U)\subset V$. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$, $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$, and give $A$ its diagonal $B$-action by multiplication [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data]. Under the affine derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], set $M=R\Gamma(U,K|_U)$ and $N=R\Gamma(U,L|_U)$ in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $R\to A$ is flat of finite presentation, $M,N$ are pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and each has finite Tor amplitude over $R$: for each $T=M,N$ there are $a_T\le b_T$ such that $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R$-module $Q$ and $i\notin[a_T,b_T]$. Write $T_1=T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B$. Restricting the diagonal, first pullback and derived internal Hom [def-pc-derived-pullback], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to $U\times_VU$ identifies them, in the derived category, with $A[0]$, $\widetilde{T_1}$ and $\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T_1)}$. The classes give maps $\gamma:A[0]\to M_1$ and $\theta:A[0]\to N_1$ whose multiplication maps $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T_1)$ are isomorphisms. For $T=M,N$ there are natural isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pc-derived-category]
$$\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,T)}\cong R\mathcal Hom_U(K|_U,\widetilde T).$$
For $T=M$ this identifies the scalar-action maps. The affine equivalence identifies morphisms $M\to N[i]$ with $K|_U\to L|_U[i]$ for every integer $i$; an isomorphism $a:M\to N$ preserves $\gamma,\theta$ if and only if its sheaf isomorphism preserves $\xi|_{U\times_SU},\eta|_{U\times_SU}$. All these identifications respect scalar multiplication, composition, and further affine open restrictions. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The affine flatness criterion applied to the specified opens gives flatness of $R\to A$. The affine-open characterization of local finite presentation gives $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ for finite $n,m$. These results apply to the original $U,V$; no shrinking, properness or Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

Do the following for $E=K,L$. Pseudo-coherence restricts to $U$ by restricting its local finite-free representatives. The pseudo-coherent quasi-coherence theorem makes $E|_U$ an object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U)$, so the affine equivalence defines $T=R\Gamma(U,E|_U)$ and $\widetilde T\cong E|_U$. The affine pseudo-coherence criterion gives a bounded-above finite-free representative of $T$. Apply the affine relative Tor-amplitude criterion to $U\to V$: the supplied local finite Tor dimension is exactly its local hypothesis. Indeed $(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S)|_U=(f|_U)^{-1}\mathcal O_V$, and restriction of a local Tor bound follows by extending test modules from a smaller open by zero. Its conclusion is one finite $R$-Tor interval for $T$, despite the initially local bounds. Testing with $Q=R$ shows that $T$ is bounded, in particular bounded below.

The presentation in step 1 gives $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]/(g(x),g(y))$, so $R\to B$ is finitely presented. Flat module base change makes $B$ flat over the first $A$; also $-\otimes_R B=(-\otimes_R A)\otimes_{A,p_1}B$ is a composite of exact functors, hence $B$ is flat over $R$. Multiplication $\mu:B\to A$ is surjective since $\mu(a\otimes1)=a$. Apply the flat finitely presented quotient pseudo-coherence lemma to $R\to B\to A$ and the finite-free complex $A[0]$. It gives pseudo-coherence of $A[0]$ over $B$, without assuming that either ring is Noetherian. For $T=M,N$, the flat-single tensor cohomology theorem (on the one-point ringed site of $A$) gives $H^i(T_1)=H^i(T)\otimes_{A,p_1}B$; thus $T_1$ is bounded below. These are the precise two hypotheses for the diagonal internal-Hom comparison.

Put $W=U\times_VU$. Since $V\hookrightarrow S$ is an open monomorphism, $W=U\times_SU$ is an open of $X\times_SX$. The affine fibre-product theorem identifies $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and its first projection with $p_1:a\mapsto a\otimes1$. The diagonal is induced by $\mu$: both composites $A\to B\to A$ are the identity. On a basic open $D(b)$ its direct-image algebra has sections $A_{\mu(b)}$. The associated-sheaf section formula for the $B$-module $A$ gives exactly these sections, actions and fraction restriction maps. Thus the restricted diagonal is $\widetilde{A[0]}$, including its algebra multiplication. The affine pullback comparison identifies the restricted $Lp_1^*E$ with $\widetilde{T_1}$, naturally also on maps.

source.place: Tag 0E2U, compatibility of diagonal pushforward and first pullback; schemes.tex Tags 01I4 and 01HV; perfect.tex Tag 08DW

proof.text: Restriction of derived internal Hom to $W$ gives the Hom of the two restricted objects. Apply the affine algebra-class evaluation comparison with coefficient ring $B$, algebra $C=A$ via $\mu$, and second object $T_1$. Step 3 verified pseudo-coherence of $C[0]$ and bounded-below cohomology of $T_1$. Its evaluation-normalized isomorphism identifies that Hom with $\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T_1)}$. Full faithfulness over $B$ gives the unique module classes $\gamma,\theta$ corresponding to $\xi|_W,\eta|_W$. To check that these classes give the required isomorphisms, use the canonical tensor comparison for open restriction: on K-flat representatives it restricts the same total-tensor maps, multiplication and unit. The open-restriction evaluation mate is invertible. Naturality of tensor--Hom transposition says that, under this mate, restriction of the transpose of $\xi\mu$ is the transpose of its restriction. Hence the supplied multiplication isomorphism restricts to the multiplication map of the restricted class. Finally the class-map identity in the affine algebra-class comparison identifies it with the sheafification of $m_\gamma$ (respectively $m_\theta$). The affine equivalence reflects invertibility, proving both algebraic multiplication maps are isomorphisms.

For $T=M,N$, apply the affine pseudo-coherent Hom theorem to $P=M$ and $T$. Step 2 gives the bounded-above finite-free first representative and bounded-below second cohomology required by its statement. This gives the asserted isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_U)$. Its normalization can be checked using the finite-free derived-Hom model on $U$ and on the one-point ringed space of $A$: choose $P^p=0$ for $p>b$ and a representative $F^q=0$ for $q<c$ of $T$. In Hom degree $n$ only $c-n\le p\le b$ contribute. Each finite-free factor identifies $\widetilde{\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^p,F^{p+n})}$ with $\mathcal Hom(\widetilde{P^p},\widetilde{F^{p+n}})$ by sending a map to its sheaf map; the finite sums and differential $d_Fh-(-1)^n h d_P$ agree. Evaluation sends $h\otimes x$ to $h(x)$ on both sides. Thus this is precisely the transpose of sheafified derived evaluation under the canonical tensor comparison. This description before choosing representatives proves naturality for derived morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom (3)(a) and its proof; cohomology.tex Tag 08I5, lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free

proof.text: At $T=M$, the algebraic scalar map is the transpose of the unit action $A[0]\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M\to M$. The evaluation normalization of step 6 sends it to the transpose of $\mathcal O_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}K|_U\to K|_U$, which is the scalar map in the definition of a supplied pair. It is also the restriction of the scalar map on $X$: the open-restriction evaluation mate identifies transposes, and the canonical tensor restriction comparison carries the unit action to the unit action. Thus the assertion identifies the actual maps, not just their targets.

source.place: Tag 0E2V, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, scalar map; cohomology.tex Tag 08DL

proof.text: The affine equivalence is fully faithful and triangulated, with target a full subcategory of $D(\mathcal O_U)$. Applying it to $M,N[i]$ gives the required Hom bijection for every integer $i$. It preserves inverses, and full faithfulness lifts an inverse and its two identity equations, so it also gives the isomorphism bijection. If $\alpha$ corresponds to $a:M\to N$, the natural affine pullback comparison identifies the sheafification of $a\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B$ with $Lp_{1,U}^*\alpha$. Steps 4--5 identify $\gamma,\theta$ with the restricted classes. Therefore sheafification of $(a\otimes^{\mathbf L}B)\gamma=\theta$ is exactly $(Lp_{1,U}^*\alpha)\xi|_W=\eta|_W$. Faithfulness over $B$ gives the converse. This proves the class-preservation equivalence.

source.place: Tags 0E2U and 0E2W, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing, affine Hom and class-preservation reduction

proof.text: The preceding choices are canonical: on representative maps, tilde sends $rh$ to $r\widetilde h$ and $gh$ to $\widetilde g\,\widetilde h$. The same identities hold on roofs, since a quasi-isomorphism is sent to an invertible map. These identities prove scalar and composition compatibility. For smaller affine opens $U'\subset U$, $V'\subset V$ with $f(U')\subset V'$, their product $W'=U'\times_{V'}U'$ is an affine open of $W$. The pullback comparison identifies restriction with derived extension of scalars on $U'$ and on $W'$. The diagonal section calculation of step 4 identifies its restricted algebra with $\mathcal O_{U'}$ pushed along its diagonal, including multiplication. For the class Hom comparison, the affine algebra-class comparison explicitly gives compatibility with every affine-open restriction, including successive ones. For the comparison of step 6, restriction of the same evaluation map and the invertible open-restriction evaluation mate give the smaller-chart comparison: both are the unique tensor--Hom transpose of that evaluation after the canonical tensor identifications. Thus scalar maps, Hom bijections and the class-preservation equation all commute with these restrictions. This applies to arbitrary affine open subcharts, not only principal ones.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, evaluation computation and open restriction; cohomology.tex Tag 08DL; duality.tex Tag 0E2U

proof.text: If $U$ is empty, $A=B=0$ and all its module and sheaf derived objects are zero; choose the interval $[0,0]$. All asserted equations and bijections are then the unique ones. For $f$ the identity on an affine scheme, $B=A$, $p_1$ is the identity, and the formulas reduce to affine realization and the ordinary tensor unit and evaluation maps. The argument nowhere assumes nonemptiness or Noetherianity.
